# `open` and `close` are methods of `ui.window`, answered where a window is an
# instance of the component: every target but html, which renders the window
# as the builtin it is marked until Phase C2 moves its pages to `nav.page`. So
# on html a method called through its `#id` has no instance to be the method
# of, and it is refused at the call rather than emitted as `details.open()`
# against nothing. bubbletea builds the one-window form of it, and gtk4 the
# two-window one.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html app.sngl
stderr 'app.sngl:8:9: `details.open\(\)` calls a method of the node `#details`, which this target does not splice where it is written'

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea -o tea one.sngl
sngl generate --lang kotlin --platform android -o droid one.sngl

sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 -o gtk4 app.sngl

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var n = 0

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.button(text="Details", @click {
        n += 1
        details.open()
    })
}

ui.window #details(title="Details") {
    ui.text(value="{n}")
}
-- one.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var n = 0

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.text(value="{n}")
    ui.button(text="Hide", @click {
        n += 1
        main.close()
    })
}
